final.question: What's worth doing again every Monday?
final.form: The weekly report as a recurring ritual — chapters named subject line, distribution, last week / this week, what changed, the numbers, flagged for follow-up, sign-off
final.object: A pad of 8 tear-off report sheets, one per job or project (Atlantico, DataTugas, Helix, FraudShield, the hackathon, Lisbon Rent Map, Meridian, AutoPilot)

swap.reason: The spine is his own confirmed history — the Helix report cut from five hours to two, AutoPilot automating his team's report — and the eight sheets are his specific pieces with their real figures.

backdrop.reason: The sheets are the content carriers and their rearrangements do the work (stack, dated line, before/after turn, wall, restack), not a decorative layer behind the text.

depth.reason: Each chapter transforms the arrangement left by the previous one, from a blank sheet through timeline and wall to a restacked pad dated today, and the order could not be shuffled.

clipart.reason: A tear-off report pad is the document he actually works from, not the trade emblem (a bar chart or tile dashboard), which the agent deliberately ranked last.

honesty.reason: Every figure and description in the final plan matches what is true, the 35% is dropped, Meridian is marked as showing nothing further, and the false title is refused.

thirty_seconds.reason: Beat 1.1 carries his name, tagline and the five-hours-to-two proof, with a nav rail and skip-to-contact link visible from the first screen.

plain_reader.reason: The opening line is plain English about saving people hours with one concrete figure, which a recruiter can follow and a practitioner would not find inflated.

judgement.summary: The plan shapes the site as Rafael's own weekly report — seven chapters built from a pad of eight sheets, one per job or project, that fan, line up as a dated timeline, turn over for the Helix five-hours-to-two before/after, spread into a wall of real figures, and restack as a sheet dated today answering "what's worth doing again every Monday?". Its weakness is a small amount of pattern-stretching to make the form fit everything: Meridian's dashboards are said to "exist to feed" a weekly report and the Atlantico internship is given a "churn team" audience, neither of which any source supports, and the plan leans on a Rent Map screenshot and a contact address it does not yet have.
